data.title: SpaceX confirmed to get a weighting boost after Nasdaq 100 rebalancing: Bloomberg
data.description:
SpaceX (SPCX) will account for a larger weighting of the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) when the quarterly rebalance of the index takes effect next week, Bloomberg reported on Saturday, confirming provisional data published by the index provider last week.

According to data obtained by Bloomberg and calculated based on the company’s last closing price, Elon Musk’s rocket, satellite, and AI company will make up 2.82% of the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) after rebalancing on Monday, a sizable increase from its current weighting of roughly 1.28%.

The publication projected a similar weighting boost for SpaceX (SPCX) last week using pro forma data published by the Nasdaq’s Global Index Watch.

Despite its market cap exceeding $2T, the Starlink owner made up a smaller weighting in the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) in July when it was added to the index, as most of its shares were locked up, limiting their public availability for trading.

As those lockups expire, the company’s free float as well as its weighting in the Nasdaq 100 (NDX) are expected to increase, prompting index funds and exchange-traded funds that track the benchmark to buy more of its shares.

data.title: Insider trades: CrowdStrike, Uber, Snowflake among notable names
data.description:

  • CrowdStrike (CRWD) director Roxanne Austin sold 50,000 shares in the price range of $237 to $238 each for a total value of about $11.88M. The transaction represented about 39.36% of her direct holdings, leaving her with 77,040 shares.

  • Canopy Growth (CGC) CFO Thomas Stewart sold 25,755 shares at $0.93 each for ~ $23,952. The sale accounted for about 4.19% of his direct holdings, leaving him with 588,412 shares.
  • Medtronic (MDT) EVP and President, Cardiovascular Skip Kill sold 1,483 shares at $93.65 each for nearly $138,883. The transaction represented about 3.40% of his direct holdings, leaving him with 42,186 shares.

data.title: Google says Gemini AI model hacked three companies in security test
data.description:
Google (GOOG) on Friday confirmed that its Gemini model gained unauthorized access to three companies in May during a review of its cybersecurity capabilities, the first known incident of the company’s AI system autonomously engaging in such an act.

The Alphabet (GOOGL) subsidiary said in a statement that Gemini accessed the outside systems by guessing login information or using credentials found in a public repository.

The incident draws parallels to a similar incident involving OpenAI (OPENAI) that has partly led to the recent safety concerns about the pace of AI advancements. In July, the ChatGPT maker said that one of its agents powered by its advanced artificial intelligence models had hacked AI software company Hugging Face during a security test.

Google (GOOGL) said it wasn’t aware of the intrusions until July, when Irregular, an AI-focused cybersecurity firm that was carrying out the tests on Gemini, reviewed its work to look for incidents similar to the one that impacted Hugging Face.

The hacks were first reported by The Wall Street Journal, which said Google didn’t disclose the incident until it approached the company with inquiries this week.

Heather Adkins, vice president for security engineering at Google (GOOG), said in the statement that Gemini assumed that the outside systems “were part of the test,” but in all three cases, the model stopped short of committing anything further after entry.

“In a standard evaluation, the model found public information online and guessed credentials to access websites it thought were part of the test,” she noted, adding, “These events highlight the importance of training powerful AI models to act responsibly.”

data.title: Crypto names climb after SEC prepares for stock tokenization, TradFi names weaken: Financials week
data.description:
Crypto-related stocks made up four of the week's top five financial sector gainers as more traditional finance names struggled.

The overall sector, as illustrated by the State Street Financial Sector SPDR ETF (XLF), dipped 2.4% for the week ended Sept. 18, a steeper decline than the S&P 500's (SPX) 0.1% tick down. The KBW Nasdaq Bank Index (BKX) took an even bigger tumble, dropping 4.9%.

The week featured the first Federal Reserve rate hike in more than three years and a move by the Securities and Exchange Commission that paves the way to allow trading of tokenized stocks. That offset the earlier setback when the Clarity Act failed to make it to the Senate floor earlier in the week. Bitcoin (BTC-USD) ended the week up ~4.8%, rising to almost $81K on Friday, its highest level since early May.

The five biggest gainers for financial stocks with market cap of over $2B were:

  • Bill Ackman's alternative asset manager, Pershing Square (PS), rising 32% for the week;
  • Hyperliquid Strategies (PURR), up 21%; 
  • Coinbase Global (COIN), jumping 11%;
  • Riot Platforms (RIOT), gaining 11%; and
  • MARA Holdings (MARA), also increasing 11%.

The five stocks that dropped the most were:

  • Enova International (ENVA), a fintech that offers installment loans, slumped 22% after the company withdrew applications related to its proposed acquisition of Grasshopper Bancorp;
  • Asset manager Lazard (LAZ) dropped 13%;
  • Insurtech firm Ethos Technologies (LIFE) sank 11%; 
  • Private equity and venture capital firm Hamilton Lane (HLNE) slid 8.6%; and
  • Wall Street giant Goldman Sachs (GS) dipped 8.5% after its CEO warned that its FICC business will be a “bit softer” compared with the prior quarter.

data.title: MS NOW says its journalists were denied entry to the White House amid Trump’s ban
data.description:
Versant Media Group’s (VSNT) MS Now said on Saturday that its journalists were denied entry to the White House, a day after President Donald Trump said he was revoking access to the network as well as CNN (WBD) and Politico, accusing the outlets of failing to cover him fairly.

The action escalated Trump’s long-running efforts to restrict news coverage by journalists he finds objectionable and is the latest test of First Amendment protections in the U.S. Trump said Friday that he was barring the news channel, along with CNN and Politico, from the White House due to what he called unfavorable coverage and “fake news.”

MS NOW said in a statement that it stands behind its journalists.

“The White House belongs to the American people, and the decisions made inside are funded by our tax dollars,” the network said in a statement Saturday. “MS NOW intends to take any and all steps necessary to defend our First Amendment rights and the essential role of independent journalism in our democracy.”

It was unclear Saturday morning whether CNN journalists were also being blocked from the White House grounds. Network correspondents are usually there on the weekends when the president is in Washington or at nearby Camp David. Trump is at the presidential retreat in Maryland this weekend.

The Associated Press contributed to this story.

Dear readers, we recognize that politics often intersect with the financial news of the day, so we invite you to click here to join the separate political discussion.

data.title: Volkswagen is said to have called for another 4,000 layoffs at Porsche
data.description:
Volkswagen (VWAGY) anticipates more than 4,000 additional job cuts at its sports car subsidiary ​Porsche (POAHY) as part of a massive restructuring drive, German business daily Handelsblatt reported on Saturday.

The German automaker’s turnaround plan calls for a reduction of "about 4,100 employees" at Porsche (POAHY) to address an overhead shortfall of about €700M ($803.8M), according to files documenting a recent agreement by Volkswagen's supervisory board.

The latest job cuts as proposed would be "in addition  to existing agreements," the newspaper said. In July, the Stuttgart-based 911 maker announced plans to cut around 9,000 global workers by 2035, including 3,900 roles previously selected for elimination.

The report on additional job cuts comes a day after Volkswagen (VLKAF) cut its 2026 profit guidance, citing, among other things, a goodwill impairment charge related to Porsche (POAHF). The parent company can only recommend, but not mandate, ​such remedies.

Earlier this month, the supervisory board of Volkswagen (VWAGY) approved a wide-ranging restructuring plan, the most extensive in the company’s 89-year history—that will include 50,000 additional job cuts in an attempt to improve efficiency and boost its competitive position.

Volkswagen (VLKAF) and Porsche (POAHF) didn’t immediately respond to requests for comments.

data.title: Anthropic weighs launching a new AI model ahead of IPO: Reuters
data.description:
Anthropic (ANTHRO) is planning to release a new AI model ahead of its much-anticipated IPO in a bid to rival OpenAI’s (OPENAI) newfound momentum in enterprise AI following the recent launch of the ChatGPT maker’s GPT-6 Astra model, Reuters reported, citing three sources familiar with the matter.

The report comes days after Anthropic (ANTHRO) CEO Dario Amodei, along with other tech CEOs, including OpenAI’s (OPENAI) Sam Altman, called for a slowdown in the pace of AI development.

In a 3,800-word essay posted last Saturday, Amodei said, "We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models,” a view that drew support from Altman and SpaceX (SPCX) CEO Elon Musk.

The company is assessing the safety of ​its next model alongside plans for the launch, according to one of the people familiar with the matter.

Another point being discussed is how to strike a balance between new model rollouts and improving the company’s profitability as investors become more focused on the timing of anticipated profits amid rising interest rates, people familiar with the company’s thinking said.

Anthropic (ANTHRO) didn’t respond to Reuters’ requests for comment.

According to the latest data from corporate expense platform Ramp, GPT-6 Astra, released earlier this month, has already accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending compared with about 8% for Anthropic’s (ANTHRO) Claude Fable.

Meta Platforms (META) has been among the top customers of Anthropic (ANTHRO). However, the social media company is looking to cut its reliance on Anthropic’s models as it focuses more on developing AI capabilities internally, people familiar with the matter said.

Anthropic (ANTHRO) weighs launching its blockbuster IPO in November, a delayed timeline compared to its prior expectations as the AI industry confronts growing calls for a slowdown in the pace of model development, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

data.title: Warner Bros. jumps on report of settlement talks with California AG
data.description:
Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) soared 8.3% in after-hours trading after a report that Paramount Skydance (PSKY) is in advanced settlement talks with California officials over a lawsuit to block the $110 billion mega media deal, according to a  WSJ report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. 

A settlement could come as soon as this weekend, according to a separate  Reuters report late Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. Independent monitoring of CNN is one of the terms in the settlement talks, as well as a commitment to the number of theatrical releases.

A spokesperson for the California Department of ​Justice said potential ​settlement talks ⁠are confidential. "We cannot confirm or deny whether settlement talks are occurring or their ​alleged substance," the spokesperson told Reuters. Paramount declined to ​comment.

A dozen state AGs, led by California, sued to block the mega media deal in July. A trial is scheduled for March on the combination. On Tuesday, a court ordered Paramount (PSKY) and California AG Rob Bonta to meet Oct. 14 to try to work on a potential settlement.

Shares of Paramount (PSKY) jumped 7.6% in after-hours trading. 

Under the terms of the merger agreement, Paramount (PSKY) must pay Warner Bros. (WBD) shareholders $650M per quarter beginning October 1. Because the trial is set for March 2027, Paramount would be required to pay $1.3B in ticking fees plus another $190M in incremental financing costs and legal fees.

data.title: Oil falls for third straight day as Saudi supply disruptions look less severe than feared
data.description:
Crude oil futures extended declines to a third consecutive session Friday, as market watchers believed the closure of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline may have a less severe impact on supply than originally feared.

While concerns remain about the Middle East war dragging on and shipping restrictions through the Strait of Hormuz, reports that the pipeline could resume partial flows within days helped oil futures pull back from four-month highs reached earlier this week.

However, repairing damaged pumping stations and fully restoring capacity could take as long as 6-8 weeks, analysts have said.

A ship-to-ship shuttle service through the strait under U.S. military protection, with oil transferred to other tankers waiting in the Gulf of Oman, reportedly could provide Saudi Arabia with another option for getting crude to buyers.

"Middle East oil flows remain surprisingly strong despite the disruption to Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline," J.P. Morgan head of global commodities strategy Natasha Kaneva said in a note, estimating total oil flows from the Middle East averaged ~17M bbl/day over the past 10 days, nearly 75% of the 2025 average.

Satellite imagery suggests the Saudis have moved 2.8M bbl/day through Hormuz over the past six days compared to just 700K bbl/day in August, the analyst said, while cautioning that the volumes could be difficult to sustain.

Meanwhile, physical premiums for oil in the North Sea, a key reference for global prices, soared to record levels Friday, after Saudi Aramco (ARMCO) told European customers they would not receive any supplies under their long-term agreements next month.

Norway's Johan Sverdrup, a grade of crude closely comparable with Saudi supplies, was offered at a premium of as much as $35/bbl above the Dated Brent physical benchmark, Bloomberg reported, after the same oil traded at a $0.60 premium less than two weeks earlier.

In the U.S., average retail prices for regular gasoline rose to $4.47/gal on Friday from $4.30 a week ago, AAA reported, while average diesel prices hit another new all-time high of $6.45/gal.

Front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for October delivery slipped 1.6% to $100.30/bbl, front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for November delivery dropped 0.9% to $103.87/bbl, while front-month Nymex October natural gas (NG1:COM) rose 0.4% to $2.912/MMBtu.

For the week, Nymex crude and Brent crude rose 0.2% and 0.7%, respectively, and Nymex natural gas gained 2.8%.

Energy stocks, as represented by the State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), declined 1.3% this week.

data.title: NASA in talks for Boeing's Starliner for 10 or more new missions - WSJ
data.description:
Boeing (BA) and NASA are in talks about using the company's Starliner vehicle to handle 10 or more new flights to low-Earth orbit in the coming years, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

The Starliner has not flown since summer 2024, when performance problems including failed thrusters that posed safety risks left two astronauts stuck on the International Space Station for months; the astronauts returned to Earth on SpaceX's Crew Dragon vehicle, eschewing the Starliner, which came back empty.

The Crew Dragon has been the only certified vehicle to carry NASA astronauts to the space station from the U.S., but SpaceX has stopped making new Dragon ships; the company has not said publicly when it plans to stop operating the ship.

NASA said Friday it awarded SpaceX three additional astronaut missions to the space station using Crew Dragon; the flights are worth an average of $315M each and run through 2030.

There are few other options for flights to low-Earth orbit; Northrop Grumman has a cargo capsule that flies to the space station for NASA, but not a human-rated one, while Russia flies vehicles to the ISS that handle crews and cargo.
